findings_qualitative.value: The optically bipolar lobe is actually a quadrupolar outflow of two overlapping bipolar outflows; two additional younger bipolar outflows (B1, B2) and an inner outflow B3 are detected.

evidence.quote: CO map shows that it is actually a quadrupolar outflow consisting of two overlapping bipolar outflows.

findings_qualitative.value: Blueshifted absorption stripes in PV maps arise from absorption by AGB shells.

evidence.quote: blueshifted absorption stripes are detected in the outflow emissions, due to absorption by a series of shells produced by a series of asymptotic giant branch (AGB) wind ejections.

claims.hypothesis: Is the optical bipolar lobe of I17150 truly bipolar?
claims.experiment: CO 3-2 intensity and velocity maps plus channel maps and PV diagrams
claims.result: Two overlapping bipolar outflows Q1 and Q2 with opposite inclinations, same age ~350 yr
claims.finding: Quadrupolar outflow, likely from simultaneous multidirectional bullets

evidence.loc: 5.3 Possible Shaping Mechanisms for the Quadrupolar Outflow
evidence.quote: Thus, the quadrupolar outflow seems to be shaped by multidirectional bullets.

claims.hypothesis: Do the younger lower-latitude outflows trace a change of ejection direction?
claims.experiment: Model dynamical ages of B1 and B2
claims.result: Ages 280 and 200 yr, decreasing with latitude
claims.finding: Could be produced by a precessing collimated fast wind

evidence.loc: 5.4 A Precessing Collimated Fast Wind Model for the Younger Outflows
evidence.quote: probably suggesting that the outflow axes have changed from high latitude to lower latitude in $\sim$ 150 yr

claims.hypothesis: What caused the absorption stripes and what are the AGB wind properties?
claims.experiment: Model the stripes with HST arc positions
claims.result: Velocity ~13 km/s inner, ~14.4 km/s outer; innermost arc ~1300 yr ago
claims.finding: Periodic AGB mass loss shells absorb outflow emission; AGB wind ended ~1300 yr ago, possibly later if an unseen inner arc exists

evidence.quote: The ejections of the AGB wind could have ended after the ejection of the innermost shell at $\sim$ 1300 yr ago.

why_this_method.value: Forward modeling of morphology, line profile, and PV structures to derive physical properties and shaping mechanism

evidence.quote: Here we derive the physical properties (including temperature, density, velocity, and the mass-loss rate) of the AGB wind and the outflows by modeling their observed intensity maps, line profile, and PV structures in CO $J=3$–2.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gas-to-dust ratio 280 rejected as it gives ~20 Msun, too big for an OH/IR star

evidence.quote: Using this ratio, we derive a shell mass of $\sim$ 20 M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$, which seems too big for an OH/IR star, like our source.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Two separate bipolar winds from two stars rejected as very unlikely

evidence.loc: 5.3 Possible Shaping Mechanisms for the Quadrupolar Outflow
evidence.quote: However, the chance of simultaneously producing two bipolar winds from two stars is very low.

limitations_admitted.value: Distance poorly constrained; AGB stripe semi-major axis cannot be clearly identified; higher sensitivity needed for velocity jump

evidence.quote: The distance to I17150 is not well constrained.

evidence.loc: 3.5.1 Expansion Velocity of the AGB Wind
evidence.quote: Further observations at higher sensitivity are needed to derive a precise value of the velocity jump from the PV diagrams.

referee_caveats_inferred: Model parameters are hand-tuned with no uncertainties or degeneracy analysis
Dynamical ages scale with the assumed 3 kpc distance (range 2.4-3.6 kpc)
Gas-to-dust ratio choice is ad hoc
Imposed symmetry and shell thickness assumptions bias derived ages and masses
